2. This is first application filed under Section 438 Cr.P.C seeking anticipatory bail, as the applicant/accused is apprehending his arrest in connection with FIR/Crime No.572/2023 dated -:
25.05.2023, registered at Police Station Bhawarkuan, District Indore (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC.

3. Prosecution story, in brief, is that complainant Ramakant and co- accused persons Brajesh,
Rajesh, Rajkumar, Manoj and Kumari Preeti Silawat are sons and daughter of the accused Lakshmi Narayan Silawat.
Late Smt. Ratan Bai Silawat was mother of co-accused persons and wife of the present applicant.
She had died on 13.09.2009.

A house No.51 situated at Manish Bagh Colony,
Indore, area 1500 sq. ft. was owned by Smt. Ratanbai.

After death of Smt. Ratanbai, the applicant Laxminarayan Silawat vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44796996/
1 and co-accused persons had filed an application for mutation in building tax register of Revenue Department Municipal Corporation, Indore.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On 25.04.2013, the present applicant had filed an application alongwith affidavit of the aforesaid house's mutation application before Revenue Department Municipal Corporation, Indore.
In the affidavit, the applicant had mentioned that if his name alone is mutated, other legal heirs have no issues.
The applicant had also filed an affidavit showing that the co-accused persons and complainant has no objection if name of the applicant Lakshmi Narayan alone is mutated.
While the complainant is one of the legal heir of the deceased and used to live in the aforesaid house.
He never gave his consent, thereby the applicant had made forged signature of the applicant in affidavit dated 15.04.2013.
After mutation, the applicant had taken loan of lakh of rupees with consent of co-accused persons.

On 30.08.2022, the applicant said to the complainant to vacate the house because co-accused Brijesh has taken loan from Chola Mandalam Finance Branch, Vijay Nagar, Indore of Rs.70,00,000/- and due to non-payment of installments, the house is being auctioned.

The applicant and co-accused persons entered into conspiracy to commit cheating with complainant, thereby the applicant had committed forgery in documents and the applicant and co-accused persons with intent to cause wrongful loss to the complainant by getting the house auctioned after non-payment of installment of the loan taken by him.
4.
Learned counsel for the applicant/accused submits that the applicant has not committed the offence and has falsely been implicated in the case.
He is a 77 years old man.
Therefore, it is prayed that the applicant be granted anticipatory bail.

5. On other hand, learned counsel for the State/non-applicant has objected the prayer and submitted that contradictory age of applicant was mentioned in the documents and prescriptions filed by the applicant.

As per some of the documents, he is 77 years of age, while a prescription of energy hospital, Indore related year 2019, age of the applicant is mentioned to be 70 years,
therefore, it is not reliable that applicant is 77 years of age.
The applicant is main accused of the incident.
The alleged forged document has been examined by handwriting expert and it was found that forged signature of the complainant was made.
Custodial interrogation of the applicant is required in the case.
Therefore, he is not entitled for anticipatory bail.

6. Having heard learned counsels for the parties, perused the case-diary also considering the facts and circumstances of the case, in view of this Court, it is not a fit case to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Resultantly, application for anticipatory bail is rejected.

(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE Shruti Laxminarayan Silawat vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44796996/
